newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay sugar prices ease despite lower sale quota.
newsitem.headline: Bombay sugar prices ease despite lower sale quota.

text.p: Bombay sugar prices on Wednesday eased despite the government announcing a lower free sale quota for next month, dealers said.
Sluggish consumer buying and reports that local millers are holding higher unsold stock out of the current month's quota kept market sentiments quiet.

In the ready delivery S-30 slid by five rupees at 1,445/1,465 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 moved down by the same margin at 1,470/1,505 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery also fell by five rupees at 1,385/1,400 rupees per quintal for the S-30 variety and at 1,405/1,425 rupees per quintal for the M-30 variety.

Dealers said the government had announced a free sale quota of 750,000 tonnes for July against 800,000 tonnes released this month. It also announced the August quota at 750,000 tonnes and September at 750,000 tonnes. Last year's quota for July was 725,000 tonnes.
